title: Velocity at top of A
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the velocity at the highest point of track A using centripetal force condition (mg = mv²/R).

title: Pressure at top of B
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the normal force (and thus pressure) at the highest point of track B using Newton's second law and work-energy theorem.

title: Height range for safety
description: Essential: Correctly determines the range of starting heights (h) that allow the cart to clear both loops and land on the air cushion between M and N.

title: Energy conservation application
description: Important: Applies the work-energy theorem correctly to relate the starting height to velocities at key points (e.g., top of A, exit at E).

title: Projectile motion analysis
description: Important: Correctly uses projectile motion equations (h = ½gt², x = v_E t) to find the required exit velocities for landing at M and N.

title: Centripetal force setup
description: Important: Correctly sets up the centripetal force equation (N + mg = mv²/r) at the top of track B to find the normal force.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Uses an incorrect sign in the centripetal force equation (e.g., mg - N = mv²/r) for the top of a loop.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Maintains consistent units (m, kg, s, N) throughout the solution without conversion errors.

title: Logical range deduction
description: Optional: Clearly states that the exit velocity must be between the values required to land at M and N, and uses this to bound the height.
